categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build 0/5: dotnet build fails with 6 errors (CS0246). The model's Components/RichTextViewComponent.cs, ImageViewComponent.cs and QuoteViewComponent.cs inherit an invented 'BlockViewComponent' and take an invented 'BlockViewComponentArgs'; neither type exists. The model saw this failure in its last build and stopped. The 10 NU190x ImageSharp warnings come from the scaffold. Front page 0/10 and posts 0/10: the site cannot boot (check: 'Umbraco did not become ready within 240s'), so nothing renders and no pages were crawled. Even with a build, the project's Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml are still the empty create-template stubs, because the real views went to the solution root. Images 1/5: the 4 provided Unsplash photos are in a 'Blog Media' folder and picked as listing and inline images, but no page serves them. Domain/publish 5/5: domain '/' (en-US) is on 'Blog Front Page', and the front page and both posts are published (uSync content: Published Default=true).

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders 8/8: richTextBlock, imageBlock and quoteBlock are elements in Blocks; blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages; siteRoot is still in Repositories. Block grid 7/7: 'Blog Block Grid' (Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid) has rich text, image (+caption) and quote (+attribution) blocks. It is the body of both page types, and the front page and posts use it. Structure 3/5: siteRoot is the only type allowed at root, siteRoot→blogFrontPage→blogPost, templates are assigned, aliases are camelCase. But blogFrontPage also allows siteRoot as a child, a leftover from its retry update-document-type call. Hygiene 5/5: no compositions; publishDate, excerpt and listingImage are real properties; no duplicate or orphaned types.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: After a 'cd ..' the model wrote its Razor into Umbraco.Bench/Views/ at the solution root, outside the web project. The project's Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml remain empty stubs, and only the 3 broken ViewComponent classes landed in the project. Judged on their merits: the misplaced page views call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "body") (1/7). The 'adapters' are Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml, not <alias>.cshtml. They hold all the markup and never call Component.InvokeAsync (0/6). The ViewComponents use a non-existent base class, have no plain models in Models/<Folder>/ and no Views/Shared/Components/*/Default.cshtml, and they don't compile (0/7). Conventions 2/5: Program.cs and appsettings.json untouched, no migrations, no .cs in Models/, frontend built to wwwroot/dist/site.css, and GetCropUrl is used in the misplaced views. But none of this is live, and the project doesn't compile. The .mcp.json diff comes from test setup.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Posts 1/6: 2 posts, each with 4 blocks (rich text, image, rich text, quote) and relevant photos. But they define MCP as the 'Model-Content-Property' pattern, an invented Umbraco architecture idea, not the Model Context Protocol. So they are inaccurate, and thin: 4 two-sentence paragraphs per post. The quotes are made-up attributions ('Umbraco Best Practices Guide'). Looks 0/4: nothing renders because the build fails. The screenshots could not be taken ('Umbraco isn't running'). The misplaced views would give a reasonable Tailwind card layout, but they are not part of the site.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Channel/order 2/3: schema, media and domain went through umbraco MCP, and pages, blocks and publishing through umbraco-editor. No DB, Management API, uSync or migrations. The order was model → content → publish → domain → stop → build → Razor → npm build → build. The recipe's restart and curl verification were skipped after the build failed. Stray 'cd ../.. && ls -la' listed the bench root outside the project; there were no reads of results/ or tests/. Report 0/2: the final report is just 'Task completed.', after a final dotnet build that failed with errors. It discloses nothing that is broken.

summary: Mistral Small built a correct schema over MCP (three blocks, a /Custom block grid, blog front page and post types) and published two posts with a domain. Then it wrote its Razor into the solution root instead of the web project, and added ViewComponents with an invented base class. The build fails, the site never boots, and the posts describe MCP as an invented 'Model-Content-Property' pattern.
strengths: Correct block set (rich text, image+caption, quote+attribution) as elements in Blocks, in a /Custom block grid used on both page types
Post metadata modelled as real properties (publishDate, excerpt, listingImage); no compositions
Provided Unsplash photos imported into the media library and picked in content
Domain '/' on the front page and all pages published
Stayed on the MCP channel throughout

issues.text: dotnet build fails with 6 CS0246 errors: Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Components/{RichText,Image,Quote}ViewComponent.cs inherit an invented 'BlockViewComponent' with 'BlockViewComponentArgs'. The site cannot boot, so https://localhost:44317/ does not respond.

Every page view, adapter and component view went to Umbraco.Bench/Views/ (solution root) instead of Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/. The project's Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml are still empty create-template stubs.

Even on its own terms the architecture is wrong. The adapters are blockgrid/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml (not <alias>.cshtml), contain all the markup and never call Component.InvokeAsync. There are no plain view models and no Views/Shared/Components/*/Default.cshtml.
The final report is just 'Task completed.' after the last dotnet build failed. It discloses nothing that is broken.

The posts define MCP as 'Model-Content-Property', an invented Umbraco pattern, not the Model Context Protocol. The content is inaccurate and thin (4 short paragraphs per post), and the quote attributions are made up.
blogFrontPage allows siteRoot as a child (uSync ContentTypes/blogfrontpage.config Structure).
The recipe's restart and curl verification steps were skipped. A stray 'cd ../.. && ls -la' listed the bench root outside the project folder.
